assessment.overall_rationale: Left P11 splits angiogenic tip-cell sprouting (L1) and TGF-β-driven CNS tip-cell specification (L2) as two related but mechanistically distinct facets, plus a separate ion-channel mechanosensing module (L3); Right P11 similarly separates tip-cell sprouting (R1), arteriovenous identity (R2), and BBB transport/mechanosensing (R3), giving strong same-core correspondence for the sprouting modules (L1-R1) and moderate-to-partial overlaps elsewhere driven by shared genes/regulators reassigned to different mechanistic roles, with L3-R3 as the next strongest match via shared Kcnj2 mechanosensing.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe sprouting angiogenesis/tip cell identity driven by Angpt2, Cxcr4, Cdc42ep3 with identical Nrp1 (promotes tip cell) and Tek (opposes, KO increases program) regulator logic.

Shares Angpt2, Cxcr4, Hopx and Tek regulator but the central mechanism shifts from tip-cell sprouting/filopodia formation to arteriovenous identity patterning, with Angpt2/Cxcr4 reassigned to venous/AV-boundary roles.
Both are brain endothelial programs but tip-cell sprouting biology shares no mechanistic, gene, or regulator overlap with BBB glutamate transport/ion-channel mechanosensing.
Both target CNS endothelial tip cell identity and share Angpt2 and Nrp1, but the driving mechanism differs (TGF-β/ALK5-specified D-tip cells vs Nrp1-Cdc42-driven filopodial sprouting).

Both concern CNS endothelial identity specification and share Angpt2 and a Tek/Nrp1-adjacent regulatory theme, but TGF-β-driven tip cell specification differs mechanistically from Notch/Rgs6-driven arteriovenous patterning.

Identical Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 regulators with the same direction (TGF-β promotes the program) anchor both modules, but the downstream output diverges from tip-cell/vascular-maturation identity to BBB transport and ion-channel mechanotransduction.
Ion channel/calcium mechanosensing genes and mechanism have no overlap with the angiogenic tip cell sprouting program.
Rgs6 is shared but used for distinct roles (GPCR/calcium signaling modulation vs Notch-dependent arterial specification), leaving only peripheral brain-EC context overlap.

Both center on Kcnj2-mediated flow-sensitive mechanotransduction in brain endothelium, with each module adding a distinct complementary facet (calcium signaling machinery vs glutamate transport/BBB integrity).
